reading.body:
Mercury Strategies filed 31 AI lobbying reports, and its largest AI clients are telecom carriers and their trade association, not AI developers.

The client list is concentrated: CTIA at 10 filings, Lumen at 8, then Verizon, AT&T, and IAC at 4 each. Telecom firms lobby on spectrum, broadband subsidy, and network regulation, and AI now sits inside those same proceedings because training and inference depend on the networks these companies own. The filings name 13 bills, all from 2025 or later, which shows the firm's AI work is recent and legislative rather than settled.

Three lobbyists carry the load: Andrew Fields and James Green at 31 filings each, Anne-Marie Kelley at 27. The counts exceed the firm's 31 total filings because multiple lobbyists appear on the same report, so these are appearances, not separate engagements.

The data does not say what position the firm argued on any bill, and the filings record only that an issue was lobbied. It also does not show spending amounts, which chamber or agency was targeted, or whether these clients coordinate. Nothing here ties the lobbying to data center siting, power procurement, or interconnection, so the link between this activity and the grid constraint on AI is not established by these numbers.

summary: MERCURY STRATEGIES, LLC filed 31 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 70131.
